# The Comet's Long Return

## Scripture
"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name." — Psalm 147:4

## Reflection
Tonight, somewhere beyond our visible horizon, a comet is completing its long journey home. Some comets take thousands of years to complete a single orbit around our sun. Generation after generation lives and dies without ever seeing the same celestial visitor twice. Yet God knows exactly when that frozen wanderer will round the bend, and He guides it back with the same precision with which He named every star.

There is something deeply comforting in that thought. We live in an age that demands immediacy—same-day delivery, instant replies, overnight success. But God works on a different timetable. The comet doesn't rush; it doesn't grow anxious about its long absence from view. It simply trusts the gravity of the One who set it in motion.

Perhaps you are in a long, quiet season—waiting for a breakthrough, a healing, a promise to be fulfilled. The night sky whispers that God's timing is not our timing. He who orchestrated the comet's thousand-year arc is equally faithful to the unfinished story of your life. You are not forgotten. You are simply in the far quadrant of your orbit, and the One who calls you by name knows exactly when you'll come back into view.

## Prayer
Father of all creation, when my season feels long and unseen, remind me that You are faithful beyond my limited sight. Just as You guide the wandering comet home, guide me through every hidden stretch of my journey. I trust Your timing, knowing that You who set the stars in motion are working all things for good. In Jesus' name, amen.
